- op=enum: enumerator names and values (e.g. to write a predicate over an enum field).

actor.description: object: label, object path, (PIE) @gamestate @pawn @controller @gameinstance @playerstate[:n] @hud, or @subsystem:Class (editor subsystems too)

class.description: class: /Script path, /Game Blueprint, Module.Class or short name

enum.description: enum: a UENUM(BlueprintType) name or UserDefinedEnum asset

include.description: object/class: glob patterns of property names to include (default all)

max_str.description: object: truncate string values to this length (default 512)

properties.description: object/class: read exactly these properties (overrides include/exclude)

tools.title: Reflect objects, classes, enums

tools.description:
Build levels from an unreal.scene/v1 spec (`path` or `json`).
- apply: create/update the spec's actors (one undo step) and save; dry_run reports the diff. Additive: matched by the scene tag, never by label alone; stale actors go via scene_clear op=prune.
- check: lint the level (lit, meshes present, PlayerStart, nav).
- preview: offline layout placements.
- env_preset: lighting/sky/exposure preset (sun always points down).

checks.description: check: {require_environment_lit, require_no_missing_meshes, require_player_start, require_nav_bounds, spawns_within_bounds: bool}

dry_run.description: apply: report add/update/missing assets without changing the level

json.description: apply/check: the spec as inline JSON (instead of path)

layout.description: preview: {type: grid|ring|line|scatter, count, spacing, rows, cols, radius, start, end, center, extent, seed}

preset.description: env_preset: daytime_clear | overcast | dusk | night | studio

scene_id.description: env_preset: scene id for the environment actors (default env)

tools.title: Declarative scenes

tools.description:
Delete actors a scene created (tagged mcp_scene:<id> only; hand-placed actors never), one undo step, then save.
- all: every actor of `scene_id`.
- prune: the scene's actors not in the spec (`path`/`json`) — after scene apply; not atomic with it.
dry_run lists them.

dry_run.description: list what would be deleted without deleting

json.description: prune: the spec as inline JSON

path.description: prune: the scene spec file (its scene_id and labels are kept)

scene_id.description: all: the scene whose actors to delete

tools.title: Remove scene actors

tools.description:
Look at the world (PNG).
- viewport: the editor world via a scene capture (works backgrounded).
- pie: the running game's screen (needs a visible viewport); HighResShot leaves out UMG/Slate UI — ui=true includes it.
- orbit: `actors` (or the level) from num_angles angles in one sheet.
Results list any map the capture actors dirtied.

actors.description: orbit: actor labels or globs to frame (default: the whole level)

fill.description: orbit: fraction of the frame the target fills (default 0.7)

location.description: viewport: camera [x, y, z] (default: the editor viewport camera)

ui.description: pie: the screen as the player sees it, UMG/Slate UI included, paused or not (plugin; a visible game viewport, at its own size)

tools.name: screenshot
tools.title: Screenshot

tools.description:
Record and compare the editor level (Saved/MCP/snapshots).
- take: store `name` (default auto): every actor's path, class, tags, transform (+ `properties`).
- diff: `name` vs `against` (default: now) → added, removed, moved, retagged, changed (by object path); unloaded World Partition actors are unknown, never removed.
- list.
- digest: quantized SHA1 of actor (scope=actors) or ISM/HISM instance transforms; stores nothing.
Put back transforms and properties with snapshot_restore.

against.description: diff: the AFTER snapshot (default: the level right now)

class_filter.description: take/digest scope=actors: only actors whose class or label contains this

limit.description: digest instances: max hashed (default 5,000,000; more fails)

mesh.description: digest scope=instances: mesh path substring filter

name.description: take: snapshot name (default auto; overwrites); diff: the BEFORE snapshot

pos_bucket.description: digest: position quantization in world units (default 1)

properties.description: take: also these properties (e.g. Health); restore resets them

tools.name: snapshot
tools.title: Level snapshots

tools.description: Move every actor that still exists back to its transform in snapshot `name` (by object path, parents first), as one undo step, then save. Transforms and the snapshot's properties only: spawned/deleted actors are listed in not_restored {added, removed, unknown (unloaded WP cells)}; for those use scene_clear or git_revert.
tools.name: snapshot_restore
tools.title: Restore a snapshot

- design: design_audit (feel, decision, style… audits), design_explore

tools.title: Toolsets and capabilities

tools.description: Step the editor's undo buffer (editor world; refused during PIE). Acts only when the next step is the server's own (title "MCP: …"): a human's edit on top is CONFLICT and nothing changes. Covers actor_edit, scene, snapshot_restore. After an undoable:false result (asset, widget, python, console edits: no undo step) undo is CONFLICT (it would revert an older edit) — use snapshot_restore or git_revert.
tools.name: undo
tools.title: Undo the server's edits

tools.description:
Editor viewport camera and selection (UI state, nothing saved).
- get: camera + game_view.
- set: location/rotation, pilot or eject, game_view.
- focus: frame `actors` (default the selection).
- select: `actors` (mode replace|add|remove|none), frame.
- selection. Console commands: use console.

actors.description: focus/select: labels or object paths (focus default: selection)

distance_scale.description: focus: multiplier on the framing distance (default 2)

game_view.description: set: Game View on/off (hides editor-only actors, like pressing G)

pilot.description: set: pilot this actor (label or object path) with the camera

pitch.description: focus: camera pitch in degrees (default -30, negative looks down)

rotation.description: set: camera [pitch, yaw, roll] in degrees

tools.name: viewport
tools.title: Editor viewport

tools.description:
Author a WidgetBlueprint's tree declaratively (create the asset with asset_create kind=widget_blueprint).
- op=compose: apply `tree` — add/update/reorder nodes, slots, props — then compile; never deletes. Re-composing the same tree is a no-op (same digest).
- op=prune: like compose, but DELETES every node absent from `tree` and the names in `remove`.
- op=compile: compile + save; returns the digest (and ends a deferred patch).
- op=bind (parent class MCPHUDWidget): `bindings` [{widget, field (reflected name, e.g. Percent), source: pawn|pc|player_state|game_state|subsystem|world_actor, path, label?, max_path?, conversion?: none|ratio|int_to_text|float_to_text|float_to_percent|format_text ({value} {max})|bool_to_visibility, format?}] — each tick the field follows the value; keyed by widget+field ({remove: true} drops one). Not during PIE.
Check the result with widget_query op=tree / op=render.

bindings.description: bind: the value bindings (see the description)

defer.description: compose mode=patch: apply without compiling until op=compile

mode.description: compose: full (default; converge the whole tree on the spec, never deleting) | patch (only the given nodes)

remove.description: prune: also remove these named nodes

tree.description: compose/prune: declarative node {name, class, slot?, props?, brush?, font?, is_variable?, children?[]}; every node named; class is a friendly name (TextBlock, ProgressBar, Image, Button, CanvasPanel, VerticalBox, Overlay, ...) or a /Script or /Game path

tools.name: widget_edit
tools.title: Author UMG widgets

tools.description:
Inspect UMG widgets.
- tree: a WidgetBlueprint's tree + digest.
- describe: the palette, or one class's props and slot type.
- render: a UserWidget class as a PNG (MCPAuthoring module).
In PIE: mount `class` on the game's screen / unmount; live_tree: the live widgets (geometry in viewport px, visibility, text; HUD bindings' state: path_unreadable = a typo, source_null = no source yet).

class.description: describe: a widget class (omit for the palette); render/mount: the UserWidget class or WidgetBlueprint; unmount/live_tree: only this class

tools.name: widget_query
tools.title: Inspect UMG widgets

tools.description:
Spatial questions (world=editor default, pie, auto; results echo it).
- line_trace / sphere_overlap: collision.
- nav_path / project_point: navigation (built navmesh).
- instances_count / instances_list: ISM/HISM instances, which actor_query cannot see.

limit.description: instances_list: max instances (default 8192; truncated:true when cut)

mesh.description: instances_*: only components whose mesh path contains this

object_types.description: sphere_overlap: world_static | world_dynamic | pawn | physics_body | vehicle | destructible (default: these six) | object_type_query_N (a project channel)

tag.description: instances_*: only ISM/HISM components with this component tag
